description: Object-oriented software development in Java from language basics through inheritance, exceptions, I/O, collections, threads and networking, building complete programs with tests from the first weeks. Taught to the depth of a leading object-oriented programming course in Java.
modelledOn: Sedgewick and Wayne, Computer Science: An Interdisciplinary Approach
outcomes: Write Java programs with correct syntax, types, control flow, methods and arrays, and run them from the command line and an IDE.
Design classes that use encapsulation, inheritance, polymorphism, interfaces and abstract classes appropriately.
Handle errors with checked and unchecked exceptions and write robust input and file handling.
Use the collections framework and generics to model data and choose the right collection.
Write multithreaded programs with correct synchronisation and use executors.
Build a networked application with sockets and HTTP and test code with JUnit.

units.title: Introduction to Java and language components
topics: The JVM, JDK and bytecode; compiling and running; IDE setup; Maven or Gradle basics
Program structure, main, packages and imports; comments and Javadoc
Primitive types, variables, literals, operators, casting; String and StringBuilder
Control flow: if, switch (including switch expressions), while, do, for, enhanced for
Input with Scanner; formatted output; command-line arguments

units.title: Methods and arrays
topics: Defining methods, parameters, return types, overloading, varargs; pass-by-value semantics
Static versus instance methods; recursion
One- and two-dimensional arrays; Arrays utility class; common algorithms on arrays
Writing unit tests with JUnit from the start

units.title: Object-oriented programming and encapsulation
topics: Classes, objects, fields, constructors, this; object references and null
Encapsulation: private fields, getters and setters, immutability, invariants
Static fields and methods, constants, enums
equals, hashCode and toString; records
Object relationships: association, aggregation, composition; UML class diagrams
Designing a class from a problem statement: a mobile-money wallet, a student register

units.title: Inheritance and polymorphism
topics: extends, super, method overriding, the Object class; protected access
Polymorphism and dynamic dispatch; casting and instanceof with pattern matching
Abstract classes and interfaces; default methods; functional interfaces and lambdas
Composition over inheritance; the Liskov substitution principle
Design patterns in Java: Strategy, Observer, Factory, Singleton

units.title: Exceptions
topics: The exception hierarchy; checked versus unchecked; try, catch, finally, multi-catch
throw and throws; custom exception classes; wrapping and chaining
try-with-resources and AutoCloseable
Designing error handling: fail fast, validate input, log and recover

units.title: Input and output
topics: Streams and readers: byte versus character streams, buffering
Reading and writing text and binary files; java.nio.file Files and Paths
Object serialisation; JSON with a library
Reading CSV data from a government open-data portal and summarising it

units.title: Generics and collections
topics: Generic classes and methods; bounded types and wildcards
List, Set, Map, Queue, Deque and their implementations; choosing by complexity
Iterators, Comparable and Comparator; sorting collections
Streams API: map, filter, reduce, collectors; Optional

units.title: Threads and concurrency
topics: Thread and Runnable; starting, joining, sleeping; thread lifecycle
Race conditions, synchronized, volatile, locks; deadlock
ExecutorService, thread pools, Future and CompletableFuture; concurrent collections
A producer-consumer example and a parallel file processor

units.title: Networking and a complete application
topics: Sockets: a TCP echo server and client; multithreaded server; UDP
HTTP from Java: HttpClient; calling a REST API and parsing JSON
URL handling, and a simple HTTP server with com.sun.net.httpserver
Project: a multi-user application (chat, quiz or inventory) with files, collections, threads, networking and tests
Packaging as a runnable JAR; documentation and code review

schedule.title: The JVM, program structure and primitive types
schedule.exercise: Write a short paragraph tracing what happens from typing javac to seeing output on screen, naming the JVM, bytecode and the class loader.

tasks.title: Write a Hello World program organised into a package, compile and run it from the command line, and explain each line including the import
Write a program that declares each primitive type, prints its size-related behaviour (overflow of a byte, truncation of a cast) and explains the result
Set up a Maven or Gradle project with one dependency, build it, and explain in writing what the build tool did that javac alone would not

schedule.title: Control flow and input
schedule.exercise: Rewrite a program that uses nested if-else chains as an equivalent switch expression, and explain why the switch version is easier to verify by inspection.

tasks.title: Write a program using if, switch and a for loop that classifies ten exam scores into grade bands and prints a summary count per band
Read a list of numbers from the console with Scanner until a sentinel value, and print their sum, average and the largest value
Debug a given loop that off-by-one skips the last element of an array, fix it, and explain why the original bound was wrong

schedule.title: Methods, arrays and unit testing
schedule.exercise: Write three JUnit test cases, including one edge case, for a method that finds the maximum value in an array before you write the method itself.

tasks.title: Write an overloaded method that computes area for a circle, rectangle and triangle, and call all three overloads from a test
Implement a method that reverses a two-dimensional array in place and verify it with JUnit tests covering a square and a non-square array
Write a recursive method to compute the nth Fibonacci number, compare it with an iterative version on timing for n equals 30, and explain the difference

schedule.title: Classes, encapsulation and object design
schedule.exercise: Design a class for a mobile-money wallet from a problem statement, choosing fields, constructors and which operations must be validated, before writing any code.

tasks.title: Write a class with private fields, a constructor and getters, create two objects and show that changing one does not affect the other
Design an immutable class representing money with validation that rejects a negative amount, and write a test proving it cannot be mutated
Add a static counter field and a named constant to a class so every object can report how many instances exist, and verify the count with a test

schedule.title: Object identity, relationships and diagrams
schedule.exercise: Draw a UML class diagram for a wallet, a transaction and a customer, correctly showing association, aggregation or composition for each relationship.

tasks.title: Override equals, hashCode and toString for a class, and show with a test that two logically equal objects are treated as equal in a HashSet
Draw a UML class diagram showing association, aggregation and composition between three given classes, justifying each relationship choice
Design and implement a student register class from a problem statement, including invariants that stop an invalid age or score being set

schedule.title: Inheritance, polymorphism and interfaces
schedule.exercise: Design an abstract class and two interfaces for a set of payment methods, and explain which behaviour belongs in the abstract class versus the interfaces.

tasks.title: Create a base class and two subclasses that override a method, and show dynamic dispatch choosing the right version at runtime
Define an interface with a default method and two implementing classes, and write a lambda that implements a functional interface for a third behaviour
Use pattern-matching instanceof to process a list of mixed shape objects polymorphically and compute the total area without a type-checking chain of ifs

schedule.title: Design patterns
schedule.exercise: Pick two design patterns (Strategy, Observer, Factory, Singleton) and explain, for a described system, which one solves its stated problem and why the other does not.

tasks.title: Refactor a class hierarchy that favours inheritance into one using composition, and show the Liskov substitution problem the original design had
Implement the Strategy pattern for a billing system choosing between two fee calculation methods at runtime, selected without modifying the billing class
Implement the Observer pattern so that three listener objects are notified when a wallet balance changes, and verify all three fire exactly once

schedule.title: Exception handling
schedule.exercise: Design a custom exception hierarchy for a banking system with at least one checked and one unchecked exception, and justify each choice.

tasks.title: Write a method that throws a checked exception, catch it with a specific catch block and a general one, and show the order they are tried
Use try-with-resources to open and automatically close a file resource, and show with a test that the resource is closed even when an exception occurs
Debug a program that silently swallows an exception and corrupts data, add proper validation and logging, and show the fixed version fails fast with a clear message

schedule.title: Files, streams and serialisation
schedule.exercise: Write a short note on when to use byte streams versus character streams, with one file type that needs each.

tasks.title: Read a text file line by line, transform each line, and write the result to a new file using java.nio.file
Serialise a list of objects to JSON with a library, then deserialise it back and confirm the result equals the original list
Read a CSV file of open-data figures, compute a summary statistic per category, and handle a row with a missing or malformed field without crashing

schedule.title: Generics and collections
schedule.exercise: Compare List, Set and Map for three described use cases and justify which collection fits each, including the expected time complexity.

tasks.title: Choose the right collection type for three described scenarios (lookup by key, unique items, insertion order) and justify each choice
Sort a list of custom objects two different ways using Comparable and a separate Comparator, and verify both orderings with a test
Write a generic method bounded to Comparable types that finds the maximum of any list, and use the Streams API to filter and collect a derived result

schedule.title: Concurrency
schedule.exercise: Explain, with a short example, how a race condition on a shared counter happens and show two different fixes (synchronized and an atomic type).

tasks.title: Start two threads that each increment a shared counter without synchronisation, show the final count is wrong, and explain why
Fix the race condition with synchronized or a lock, and show with a test that the final count is now always correct across repeated runs
Build a producer-consumer pipeline using an ExecutorService and a blocking queue, and verify every produced item is eventually consumed exactly once

schedule.title: Networking
schedule.exercise: Compare TCP and UDP for a chat application and a sensor-reading broadcast, and justify which protocol fits each use case.

tasks.title: Write a TCP echo server and client that exchange messages, then extend the server to handle multiple clients with threads
Use HttpClient to call a public REST API, parse the JSON response, and print three extracted fields
Write a simple HTTP server with com.sun.net.httpserver that serves one JSON endpoint, and test it by calling it from a separate client program

schedule.title: Final project and packaging
schedule.exercise: Write a one-page design for a multi-user chat, quiz or inventory application, listing its classes, the collections and threads it needs, and its test plan.

tasks.title: Design and implement a multi-user application combining files, collections, threads and networking, with JUnit tests for its core logic
Add a test suite covering at least one concurrency scenario and one networking scenario for the built multi-user application
Package the finished application as a runnable JAR with manifest and documentation, and verify it runs correctly on a clean checkout
